Mom crushed a clove.

more.def: One small section of a garlic bulb, or a dried flower bud used as a spice.
examples: Mom crushed a clove of garlic for the sauce.
The ham was studded with cloves.
The cookies had cloves in them.

easy.def: A small plant with three round leaves.
examples: I found a clover.
The grass has clover.
A four-leaf clover is lucky.

more.def: A small plant with leaves in groups of three and small round flowers; a four-leaf kind is thought to bring good luck.
examples: We searched the grass for a four-leaf clover.
Bees love the sweet flowers of the clover.
Cows ate the clover in the field.

easy.def: A funny circus performer with a painted face.
examples: The clown made us laugh.
The clown has a big red nose.
A clown juggled at the party.

more.def: A performer who wears a funny costume and makes people laugh.
examples: The clown juggled balls at the circus.
A clown with a red nose gave balloons to the children.
The class laughed at the clown's silly tricks.

easy.def: A group of people who meet for fun.
examples: I joined the art club.
Our club meets on Friday.
Do you like the chess club?

more.def: A group of people who meet to share something they like.
examples: She joined the book club at school.
The hiking club meets every Saturday.
Our club has ten members.

easy.def: A stick for hitting a ball in golf.
examples: Dad swung the club.
He bought a new club.
She hit the ball with a club.

more.def: A long stick with a shaped end used to hit the ball in golf.
examples: He chose a different club for the long shot.
She swung the club and the ball sailed away.
Golf clubs are kept in a bag.

easy.def: A small building where a club meets.
examples: We met at the clubhouse.
The clubhouse is in the yard.
We built a clubhouse.

more.def: A building or a room where the members of a club meet, or a small hideout that kids build.
examples: The kids built a clubhouse in the backyard out of old boards.
The golf club has a large clubhouse with a snack bar.
We held our club meeting in the clubhouse.

easy.def: To make the sound a hen makes.
examples: The hen clucked.
Chickens cluck.
I heard it cluck.

more.def: To make the short, low sound that a hen makes.
examples: The hen clucked as she led her chicks across the yard.
Chickens cluck softly when they are happy.
The hens clucked and pecked at the grain.

easy.def: The sound a hen makes.
examples: I heard a cluck.
The cluck of the hen.
A cluck came from the coop.

more.def: The short, low sound that a hen makes.
examples: We heard the cluck of the hens in the barn.
A cluck came from the nest.
She imitated the cluck of a chicken.

easy.def: A hint that helps you find an answer.
examples: The footprint was a clue.
I found a clue.
This clue helps solve it.

more.def: A fact or object that helps you solve a puzzle or mystery.
examples: The muddy footprints were a clue to who had been in the kitchen.
The word puzzle has a clue for every box.
The detective found a clue in the garden.

easy.def: Not knowing anything about something.
examples: I was clueless.
He was clueless about the plan.
She felt clueless.

more.def: Having no idea about something, or not understanding what is going on.
examples: I was clueless about how to play the new game.
He was clueless about the surprise party.
She felt clueless on her first day at the new school.

easy.def: A small group of things stuck together.
examples: A clump of grass.
A clump of mud.
A clump of trees.

more.def: A small group of things growing or stuck closely together.
examples: A clump of grass grew by the rock.
A clump of mud fell off my shoe.
A clump of trees stood in the field.

easy.def: Not good at moving carefully.
examples: I am clumsy.
The clumsy puppy fell.
A clumsy boy tripped.

more.def: Awkward and likely to bump into or break things.
examples: The clumsy puppy tripped over its paws.
I am clumsy when I carry a lot of plates.
A clumsy mistake spilled the milk.

easy.def: A small group of things close together.
examples: A cluster of grapes.
A cluster of stars.
A cluster of flowers.

more.def: A small group of things that grow or are gathered close together.
examples: A cluster of grapes hung from the vine.
We saw a cluster of stars in the night sky.
A cluster of kids stood by the door.

easy.def: To gather close together.
examples: The kids clustered around.
Birds cluster on the wire.
We clustered together.

more.def: To gather or grow close together in a small group.
examples: The children clustered around the teacher to hear the story.
Penguins cluster together to keep warm.
The houses cluster around the small village green.

easy.def: To hold something tightly.
examples: I clutch my teddy bear.
She clutched her bag.
The baby clutched my finger.

more.def: To grab and hold something tightly, often because you are scared or want to keep it safe.
examples: She clutched her backpack as the train rushed by.
The baby clutched my finger with her tiny hand.
He clutched the railing as the boat rocked.

easy.def: A small bag that you hold in your hand.
examples: She carried a small clutch.
The clutch was shiny.
Her clutch had a mirror in it.

more.def: A small purse without a strap that is held in the hand.
examples: She carried a small silver clutch to the party.
The clutch held her phone and a lipstick.
He picked up her clutch from the chair.

easy.def: A group of eggs laid at one time.
examples: A clutch of eggs is in the nest.
The hen laid a clutch.
We found a clutch of eggs.

more.def: A group of eggs that a bird or reptile lays at one time.
examples: A clutch of three blue eggs lay in the nest.
The turtle laid a clutch of eggs in the sand.
The hen sat patiently on her clutch of eggs.

easy.def: A messy pile of things.
examples: My room is full of clutter.
The clutter is everywhere.
Clean up the clutter.

more.def: A messy collection of things that are left lying around.
examples: My desk was covered with clutter, so I tidied it.
The clutter in the garage made it hard to find the bikes.
We cleared the clutter off the table before dinner.
